items.title: EFF: Flock Safety ALPR Surveillance Report
items.summary: EFF's investigation finds Flock Safety operates ALPRs in 4,000+ communities with broad data-sharing agreements. Civil liberties concerns center on retention duration, opaque sharing protocols, and the absence of judicial oversight for queries.
key_claims: Flock Safety operates in over 4,000 communities.
Default data-sharing agreements include local and federal partners.
EFF cites the lack of judicial oversight as a primary civil liberties concern.

items.title: Flock Safety -- Transparency Report
items.summary: Flock Safety's official transparency report describes a default 30-day data retention window and partnerships with law enforcement agencies. The report frames the program as opt-in for participating jurisdictions.
key_claims: Jurisdictions opt in to law enforcement data sharing.
Transparency reporting is published on a recurring cadence.

items.title: Brookings: Policy Tradeoffs of License Plate Readers
items.summary: Brookings reviews ALPR policy across jurisdictions and identifies a tradeoff between investigative utility and bulk-surveillance risk. Stricter retention windows correlate with lower civil liberties friction but reduce cold-case clearance.
key_claims: Retention duration is the dominant policy variable.
Shorter retention reduces civil liberties friction.
Investigative utility declines as retention shrinks.
